name: Acyclovir
summary: Acyclovir is cleared by the kidneys, so the US labels lengthen the dosing interval (oral) or lower the dose and interval (intravenous, IV) by creatinine clearance (CrCl), and add a dose after each hemodialysis session. Oral and IV tables differ; do not transpose doses. IV: infuse over at least 1 hour (renal tubular damage), keep the patient well hydrated (acyclovir can precipitate in the renal tubules), and dose obese patients by ideal body weight (label).
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73 m2).

bands.recommendation: Oral: usual dosing. IV: usual dose every 8 hours (label: CrCl >50).
Oral: no change for 200 mg or 400 mg regimens (CrCl >10) or 800 mg five times daily (CrCl >25) (label). IV: CrCl >50, every 8 hours; CrCl 25–50, 100% of the dose every 12 hours (label).

Oral: 800 mg every 4 hours regimen: CrCl 10–25, 800 mg every 8 hours; 200 mg and 400 mg regimens unchanged (CrCl >10) (label). IV: CrCl 25–29, every 12 hours; CrCl 10–25, 100% of the dose every 24 hours (label).

Oral: CrCl 10–25, 800 mg every 8 hours; CrCl 0–10, 200 mg every 12 hours (200 mg and 400 mg regimens) or 800 mg every 12 hours (800 mg regimen). IV: CrCl 10–25, 100% of the dose every 24 hours; CrCl 0–10, 50% of the dose every 24 hours (label). Neurotoxicity can occur even at adjusted doses.

hd.text: Oral: use the CrCl 0–10 regimen (200 mg every 12 hours for the 200 mg and 400 mg regimens; 800 mg every 12 hours for the 800 mg regimen). IV: 50% of the dose every 24 hours (CrCl 0–10). Schedule a dose right after each dialysis; a 6-hour session lowers levels by about 60% (label). Watch for neurotoxicity (confusion, hallucinations, seizures), which can occur even at adjusted doses.
hd.short: CrCl<10 dose; give a dose after HD

pd.text: No supplemental dose needed after adjusting the interval (oral and IV labels).

crrt.text: Not in the labels. Published CRRT regimen (IV): 5 to 7.5 mg/kg every 24 hours; therapeutic drug monitoring where available (Li 2020).

dialyzable: Yes: half-life about 5 hours during hemodialysis (label).
monitoring: Kidney function and hydration. Neurotoxicity (confusion, hallucinations, dysarthria, seizures) is most common in end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and older adults, including at adjusted doses; stop the drug and consider hemodialysis if it occurs.

pediatric.approved_ages: Oral: not established under 2 years (oral label). IV: from birth (neonatal HSV) and for children under 12 years with HSV or varicella-zoster infections (IV label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Oral chickenpox, 2 years and older: 20 mg/kg 4 times daily for 5 days. IV, under 12 years: mucocutaneous HSV in immunocompromised 10 mg/kg every 8 hours for 7 days; HSV encephalitis (3 months to 12 years) 20 mg/kg every 8 hours for 10 days; varicella-zoster in immunocompromised 20 mg/kg every 8 hours for 7 days (labels).
pediatric.max_dose: Oral: over 40 kg, adult dose. IV: never more than 20 mg/kg every 8 hours for any patient (IV label).

renal.recommendation: Normal kidney function: usual pediatric dosing (label).

IV label table (CrCl in mL/min/1.73 m2, not restricted by age): 25–50, 100% every 12 hours; 10–25, 100% every 24 hours; 0–10, 50% every 24 hours. Neither label states pediatric validation; specialist input.

hd.text: No pediatric data in label. Specialist input.

pediatric.neonates: Neonatal HSV, birth to 3 months (IV): 10 mg/kg every 8 hours for 10 days; 15 or 20 mg/kg every 8 hours has been used, but its safety and efficacy are not known (IV label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
